pipeline: Van Gogh Neural offline CV pipeline

source_image.note: Vincent van Gogh, The Starry Night (1889), MoMA

depth.convention: grayscale value 255 = nearest (village band), 0 = farthest (moon/stars). Raw model output preserved, min-max normalized.

flow.method: RAFT flow between the original painting and a synthetic next frame warped by vortex displacement fields centered on auto-detected luminous elements (moon + stars)

encoding.flo: Middlebury float32, u then v per pixel, full 1280x1014
encoding.rgb_png: R = u/(32)+0.5, G = v/(32)+0.5, B = |f|/16; value 128 = zero flow, clamped

layers.sky: complement of all other layers (masks partition the image, sum = 100%)

consumes.depth: uDepth -> pointer parallax + slow auto-drift, strength uParallax=0.045
consumes.flow: uFlow (flow_raft_rgb.png) -> time-modulated swirl advection, decode flow_px = (texel.rg - 0.5) * 32.0, gain uFlowAmp=2.2
consumes.layers: six mask textures -> per-layer motion amplitude {sky:1.0, moon:0.30, stars:0.45, cypress:0.70, village:0.22, mountains:0.40} + star twinkle

web_demo.fallback: if any asset fails to load, main.js degrades to the original wave shader (the page never breaks)

regeneration: see cv_pipeline/scripts/*.py (paths are machine-local; adapt SRC/OUT_DIR if re-running)
